steps.title: Organisation
steps.body: Dossiq handles cases from intake to archive for your organisation. Its name and logo are kept on the organisation in OpenRegister, so every app shows the same ones. Leave a field blank to keep what is there.

steps.title: House style
steps.body: The house style comes from Thematiq. Choose your organisation's token set in the Thematiq administration settings; Dossiq follows it straight away.

steps.title: Case types
steps.body: Switch on the case types you work with. Each card installs its own set; the case types every instance needs are already there.

steps.title: Example data
steps.body: Want to look around with example cases first? You can delete them afterwards.
steps.note: Example data uses fictional people and organisations only.

steps.title: Welcome to Dossiq
steps.body: In seven steps you register your first case and see where it goes. The case you save is a real record, not a demo.

steps.title: All your cases
steps.body: You work from this list: the open cases in your teams.
steps.task: Click All cases in the menu

steps.title: Register a case
steps.body: Register your first case. Give it a title, pick a case type, then save. You can add tasks, decisions and documents later.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.title: Where case types come from
steps.body: Every case follows a case type, its blueprint. The case type decides the statuses a case moves through, how long it may take, who handles it and what may be decided. Have a look. You do not need to make one: dossiq ships with a set of them.

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a deadline that warns before it passes, a confirmation that goes out on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.

steps.title: Your own work
steps.body: Your work lives here: today's tasks, deadlines and open cases in one place.

steps.title: Your first case is on the dashboard

config._userWidgetsNote: REQ-DASH-031 (archived as REQ-DASH-024), my-teams-queue. Each preset carries its own register, schema and filter, so adding one asks the reader for nothing they do not have: a user has neither a register nor a schema in front of them, and a widget type that asks for one arrives as a blank card rather than a refusal. `_watching` is OpenRegister's own per-reader lens, the same one the Followed chip and the My Work tile read, so the three cannot disagree. The second preset is the unclaimed work of the reader's OWN teams: the Queue page's filter plus `assignedGroup: @myGroups`. A team is a Nextcloud group (one-team-model), and `@myGroups` (nextcloud-vue, nextcloud-group-surfaces) resolves to the ids of the groups the reader is in, sent as an IN filter (`assignedGroup[]=a&assignedGroup[]=b`, which OpenRegister's MagicSearchHandler turns into `assignedGroup IN (...)`). While the groups load, and for a reader in no group, the token stays unresolved and the list does not fetch but shows its `prompt`: OpenRegister reads an EMPTY IN list as no condition at all, so sending one would show every team's work to a person in no team. Until the nextcloud-vue release that carries `@myGroups` is installed, the token is unknown to the library and the list shows its prompt, never the wrong cases.

widgets.title: Recently opened
widgets._note: case-number-and-favourites, row 2.19. What this reader opened last, over OpenRegister's `_recent` lens, which carries its own order (last view descending) and keeps the last hundred. Deliberately NO `order` of its own: an order declared here would override the one thing the lens is for and the tile would answer a different question from its chip. Deliberately no status filter either, for the reason the chip carries none: this answers 'what was I just looking at'. The muted date column reads `@self.viewedAt`, the ISO 8601 moment this reader last opened the case, which the `_recent` lens adds to the metadata envelope of each object it returns. When OpenRegister reports `@self.lenses.recent.available: false`, CnDataTable shows the matching `lensReasonTexts` entry instead of `emptyText` (nextcloud-vue#1421); the values are English source keys, translated through dossiq's own catalogue like `emptyText`.

The tile is four grid columns (about 340px), and three columns (number, title, date) asked for about 490px, so the date, the one column that says when, was cut off on the right. The board DqDashboard draws this tile as two columns: the title with the case number as a muted line under it, and the date on the right. So the number is the title's `secondary` line, the title wraps (`cn-cell--wrap`) instead of pushing the table wider, and the date keeps one line at the end. No widths are declared: the tile hides its header, and a width only reaches a table through its header cells.

content._viewAllNote: one-case-list A22, triage item 4. The query is this table's OWN filter in the flat bracket grammar, key for key, and `dashboardViewAllRoutes.spec.js` holds that invariant for every tile: a table that counts one set of cases and a View all that lands on another is the dropped filter this fixes. The nested `{ deadline: { lte } }` form belongs in a `source.filter`, which the widget reads, and NOT in a route query, which `buildQueryString` would JSON-stringify into a literal object string that matches nothing. Note the WINDOW: this table is overdue AND due within three days, wider than the Cases page's Overdue chip, so it deliberately does not carry that chip's filter. `kpi-overdue` is the widget whose count the Overdue chip reproduces exactly, and that equality is asserted. CnIndexPage merges the query into the fetch under the page's own filter, so the filter arrives and the list is right; what it does NOT do is activate a matching chip, because `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` reads only `default`. The reader lands on All with the query applied and no chip showing why, and naming a chip from a query needs a nextcloud-vue change.

pages.title: Your queue
pages._note: Everything waiting on the reader, in one place, fed by the declared queue sources. A dashboard page with ONE `work-queue` widget (the library's CnWorkQueue) and not type:"index": an index page names one register and one schema, and this list spans cases, engine tasks, consultations, advice requests, mentions, work covered for an absent colleague, and calendar items the reader planned for themselves. No manifest key names a set that crosses four stores and a calendar. It is also not a second index over (dossiq, case), so gate-68 has nothing to answer: the page never reads the case schema directly. READ THE NAME COLLISION: the team queue is the UNCLAIMED POOL, every open case nobody has picked up, a view of the Cases page; this one is personal and nobody else can see it. The page names NO source. Every group, its heading and the sentence saying what closes it come from the server, which builds them from the declared queue sources, so a ninth mechanism reaches this page by declaring itself rather than by an edit here. Plan an item opens the library's CnActionDialog, which posts the item and fires `cn:page:refresh`; the work queue listens on that channel, so the planned item shows at once.

pages.title: Cases
pages._note: `excludeFields: [status]` keeps the status picker OFF this page's form dialog, and the reason is not cosmetic. On CREATE the picker listed every case type's statuses. CnFormDialog loads a reference field's options once, at open time, and `status` carries `x-relation-filter: { caseType: "@object.caseType" }`: a token that resolves to nothing while the form is still empty, so the fetch goes out unfiltered and never goes out again. Half those options are named `Received` or `In progress`, belong to a different case type, and are therefore both indistinguishable and wrong. A case is born with its own case type's `initialStatus` through `x-openregister-prefill`, so there is no status a person should be picking here at all. On EDIT the token does resolve and the picker is correctly scoped, but a raw dropdown writes the field straight through: no statusRecord, no guard evaluation, none of the transition's `automaticActions`. A status is the OUTPUT of a transition, not a field. CaseDetail's `lifecycleActions.field: status` is where one changes.

config._showUnreadRowsNote: unread-state-on-the-case, task 1.1. An unread row reads in bold with the library's unread marker (CnDataTable, from `@self.unread`, which OpenRegister attaches per reader on the render path). The board look marks unread rows only on a page that asks, and this page asks: its Unread chip (`_unread`, resolved inside the query) is one of its own quick filters, so it does not use `personalLenses`. An absent flag reads as read, because `@self.unread` is omitted for an anonymous read.
config._rowIndicatorsNote: lifecycle-acts-on-the-case, REQ-LIFE-13 and REQ-LIFE-15. Incomplete, on hold (held until a later date) and draft ride the title cell as icons, each with its word as hidden text and tooltip (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1), instead of a column that is empty on nine rows in ten. A row in none of the three states says nothing at all. An unreadable `heldUntil` reads as not held.
config._allowExportNote: case-list-export-via-or-export-leaf. The library's own Export menu (CSV and Excel) on the actions bar; it shows because the case schema is flagged `exportable` in lib/Settings/dossiq_register.json. A click sends the browser to OpenRegister's export leaf with the query the list itself sends (search, sort, facets, the active lens and the case-type folder, without paging), so the file holds the rows the table is filtered to and OpenRegister enforces access as the reader. dossiq serialises nothing (ADR-022).
config._fieldFiltersNote: case-type-fields-filter-the-case-list, row 9.2. The values a handler narrows by are the case's own answers in `properties[]` (`{ propertyDefinition, name, value }`, written by the case form), so the query is openregister's `_element[properties][…]` (array-element-filters): one element that is both the definition and passes the value test (DQ-REINT 23 Oct: the earlier `_related[caseProperty]` read rows nothing writes, 0 on :8080 against 14 cases with answers). The bar renders ONLY when the folder sidebar has narrowed to one case type, because the fields belong to one type: offering every type's fields at once offers a list nobody can read and a query that matches nothing, since two definitions from two case types can never both be satisfied by one case. The library's CnRelatedFieldFilters draws it beside the search (`relatedFieldFilters`, `related.element`), names a refused block's field under the bar, and feeds the list's fetch through `sidebarState.onFilterChange`, since the index page drops `_`-prefixed route keys.
config._bulkBandViewsNote: DqWerkbord: over the board the bulk band counts the selected cards and offers the status move and a way out ("1 zaak geselecteerd · Status wijzigen · Annuleren"), only while cards are selected. The other bulk acts stay in the table and card views' band.
config._viewCountsNote: DqFilterBeheren: every saved view in the side panel carries its number of cases. One count request per view, grouped where views filter the same field (nextcloud-vue fetchFilterCounts).
config._bulkActionsNote: bulk-actions-report-progress. Every entry here hands its act to OpenRegister's bulk job and none of them loops. dossiq declares what happens to ONE case (lib/BulkAction/), the job walks the selection, records what it did to each case and reports it, and the dialog renders that: the progress, the per-row outcome, the skip list, the report and the stop button. A handler reads what was skipped and why BEFORE committing, because the job is rehearsed first and nothing is written until the commit. WHAT THIS REPLACES, since the shape is the point. The five entries used to call dossiq endpoints that looped server-side. Closing the tab mid-run left the selection in a state nobody could read afterwards, and the only record of what was skipped was a summary that vanished with the dialog. THE REASON IS REQUIRED on Reassign, Suspend, Resume and Extend term. The first is a case policy (reassigning four hundred statutory cases with nothing recorded about why is an audit finding waiting to happen); the other three are statutory acts under Awb 4:5 and 4:14 somebody accounts for later. The bulk action declares the requirement, the hand-off enforces it, and the disabled button says so before the click. The handlers are FUNCTIONS in src/utils/caseBulkActions.js, registered in src/registry.js as `kind: 'handler'` entries, not the declarative `handler: "open-modal"` path: that path emits an `open-modal` event nothing in the library listens for, so declaring it would ship a bulk action that does nothing when clicked. They are async now, because each one reads the list's current filters and asks OpenRegister how many cases the search matches, which is what lets the dialog say whether you have this page or the whole result. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (hydra gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all rather than a fallback glyph.

config._filterLabelsNote: How the Active line names a filter, also one that came from a link (`/cases?isFinalStatus=false`). Without it the chip read the schema's own words, "Is Final Status: false"; the board DqZaken draws "Status: lopend". `deadline` with `relative` names a range from today in words: the view Termijn deze week (deadline from @today, before @today+7d) reads "Termijn: binnen 7 dagen" (board DqFilterInMenu). `hidden` marks a working-list rule every view carries (not a draft, not a template, status not hidden in lists): the line under a saved view in Weergaven in mijn menu and the side panel leaves it out (DqPersoonlijkeInstellingen), the Active line still names it. `waitingOnApplicant` reads "Status: wacht op inwoner" and `assignee` "Behandelaar" as the column does (DqFilterBewerken, DqFilterInMenu).

The conditions are the chips' own: the same flat `deadline[lt]` / `deadline[gte]` keys with `@today` tokens, the same working-list rule `statusHiddenInLists: false`.

config._boardNote: dqwerkbord-as-the-cases-board. The Werkbord is this list in board view (board DqWerkbord), not a page of its own. A case's status references a statusType row and every case type has its own rows, so the columns come from those rows, merged by name and narrowed to one case type while the list is filtered on one. A drop resolves to the statusType row of the case's own case type and moves the case through `moveCaseStatus`, the status-transition engine, never a PATCH of `status`; `caseStatusTargets` asks the engine where a case may go and what holds it, so the board fades the rest and names the guard. A status type's `capacity` is the column's limit; final statuses are filtered out, so none of them carries one onto the board. The case type and handler columns are read-only: a drag does not change a case type, and handing a case over asks for the reason the bulk Reassign collects.

board.hint: One column per value of the property. Drag a card to change its status.

mapConfig._parityNote: What the retired /map page did, now as configuration: every case that matches the filters is plotted (up to 500, with a note past that), each marker takes the colour of its status type, as the board's columns do, and a line says how many cases have a place.
mapConfig._basemapNote: EVERY ENTRY CARRIES `options.referrerPolicy` AND MUST KEEP IT. Nextcloud sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on every page (server/lib/OC.php), Leaflet draws a tile as a plain ``, and OpenStreetMap's CDN answers a refererless tile request with an "App is not following the tile usage policy" image carrying `x-blocked: Access denied` — a grey map rather than an error, which is why it reads as working-but-empty. An ``-level policy overrides the document's, and `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` sends the instance origin but never the path, which is where a case id would be. nextcloud-vue's CnMapWidget defaults the same value, so this is belt-and-braces for as long as dossiq resolves a library release that predates that default. THE `{s}` SUBDOMAIN FORM IS ALSO LOAD-BEARING: MapCspRegistrar allowlists `https://*.tile.openstreetmap.org`, and a CSP wildcard does NOT match the bare host, so rewriting these to OSM's modern `tile.openstreetmap.org` would trade a policy block for a CSP block.

config._claimNote: The Claim row action is the same one the Queue carries (case-claim-action, row 2.4), reachable from every lens rather than only from Unclaimed. It is no longer offered on a row that already has a handler: CnRowActions reads a declarative `visibleWhen` against the row as of nextcloud-vue 2.39.0, where before this only a `visible` FUNCTION could decide per row and a JSON manifest cannot hold one. `empty` is its own operator because an unclaimed case arrives as null, '' or absent depending on the store. A claim on a case that is already somebody's is still refused by the endpoint with a sentence, which is now the backstop rather than the only guard.
config._teamColumnNote: one-team-model, my-teams-queue. `assignedGroup` holds a Nextcloud group id, so the Team column reads the field itself: nothing to expand, and the server can sort a flat string. It used to be a $ref to an organisatieRol read through `extend` as `assignedGroup.roleName`, while the handover wrote group ids into the same field, so the column showed a name for some cases and nothing for the rest. `widget: group` is nextcloud-vue's group cell (nextcloud-group-surfaces): it shows the group's display name, looked up once per group id per page, and the id while the name loads or when the group cannot be found. The library also picks it on its own for a property marked `referenceType: nextcloud-group`; the column names it so the intent reads here. It stays sortable on the stored id. The Team FACET comes from `facetable: true` on the property and counts group ids.
config._quickFiltersNote: one-case-list, D1 revised: the Queue page and the My Work page stay exactly as they are, and no menu entry changes. These chips only add the lenses to the list that already exists. Unclaimed carries the SAME two conditions as Queue's base filter (`assignee: "IS NULL"`, `isFinalStatus: false`), literally equal so the two lists cannot drift; the manifest vitest asserts that equality rather than trusting it. ALL IS THE DEFAULT, not Mine: `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` activates the chip marked `default` (and the FIRST chip when none is), so a Mine default would silently narrow every reader's first paint to their own cases and make an empty list look like an empty register. Ruben's revision to the change's own 'Mine is the default' decision; the same pattern parties-on-the-case established. Overdue spells its operator as the flat `deadline[lt]` key, not the nested `{ deadline: { lt } }` object: `buildQueryString` JSON-stringifies a nested object value, which reaches the API as the literal string `{"lt":"@today"}` and matches nothing. `@today` resolves client-side to `YYYY-MM-DD` at fetch time. Due this week (lists-that-answer) is the half-open window `[@today, @today+7d)`, written as TWO flat keys on the same field: OpenRegister's MagicSearchHandler reads `gte` and `lt` in separate `isset` branches and ANDs them, and PHP parses `deadline[gte]=` and `deadline[lt]=` into one nested array, so the pair survives the trip. `lt` rather than `lte` on the far edge, so a case due on day seven belongs to next week's chip and not to two chips at once. lifecycle-acts-on-the-case REQ-LIFE-01: every WORKING lens now carries `statusHiddenInLists: false`, not only All. A status an administrator marked hidden used to empty one chip and leave the same cases filling Overdue, Due this week, Mine, Unclaimed, the Queue, My Work and the dashboard tiles beside it, so the list and the count disagreed and neither said why. Two lenses deliberately do NOT carry it. Closed is the lens a person explicitly filtered onto the terminal statuses, and hidden statuses are mostly those, so filtering there would empty the one list that is supposed to hold them. The same reasoning keeps it off the Completed this month tile. Hidden means out of the WORKING list, never out of search and never off the case's own page.

quickFilters.label: Waiting on the applicant
quickFilters._note: aanvullingsverzoek-as-a-record, row 1.17. `waitingOnApplicant` is a derived boolean the ask writes and the answer clears, so the chip is a query rather than a reading of timers. It is a READ CONVENIENCE and not a second truth: the COUNT comes from the aanvullingsverzoek rows themselves, which is why the case page shows the days from the request and not from this field. Deliberately not `isIncomplete`, which is a different fact: that one is about required fields a handler knowingly left empty at intake, this one is about something the APPLICANT still owes.

quickFilters.label: Needs attention
quickFilters._note: markers-and-assessments-on-the-case, row 2.36. `needsAttention` is a stored, facetable boolean derived from the flag history on every save, so the chip is a real narrowing of the query rather than a search through tags. Deliberately not `_unread`: that one is per reader and clears because somebody looked, this one is the flag a named person raised and only another named person with a written reason can clear.

quickFilters.label: Following
quickFilters._note: one-follow-control: the ONE lens for the cases you keep an eye on. The Favourites chip that sat beside it is gone, because a favourite is a follow with notifications off (openregister merge-follow-and-favourites), and `_favourite` now answers exactly what `_watching` answers. case-followers, row 13.18. `_watching` is OpenRegister's own lens (object-watchers), resolved INSIDE the query the way `_unread` and `_favourite` are, so the page, the total and the facets cannot disagree. It is per reader and it is not a field of the case: the subscription lives in openregister_watchers keyed by (user, object), so nothing about it is on the case row. It is a LENS and not a filter: it narrows the id set to this reader's subscriptions and lets every other filter, the RBAC gate and the paging run over what is left, so a reader who follows nothing gets an honest empty page rather than the whole register. It carries `statusHiddenInLists` and `isDraft` for the reason every working lens does, and NOT `isFinalStatus`: you follow a case to hear how it ends, so the one that just closed is exactly the one you were waiting for. It sits beside Favourites, behind the '⋯' chip rather than in the strip: the four pills are the lenses a handler reaches for every morning, and this one answers which cases you chose to keep an eye on.

quickFilters.label: Recently opened
quickFilters._note: case-number-and-favourites, row 2.19. `_recent` is the second OpenRegister lens, over the per-user view history the platform writes when you open an object's detail, ordered by last view descending and kept to the last hundred. Deliberately no `_order` of its own: the lens already carries its order, and a sort key declared here would override the one thing the lens is for. No `isDraft` or `statusHiddenInLists` either: this list answers 'what was I just looking at', and a case you opened five minutes ago dropping out of it because an administrator hid its status is a list that lies about your own morning.

quickFilters.label: Assessed high risk
quickFilters._note: markers-and-assessments-on-the-case, row 2.40. `riskLevel` carries the same declared read rule as the assessment it mirrors, so for a reader without the `dossiq-risk-assessment` group OpenRegister filters the property out and this chip narrows to nothing. That is the right answer: an empty list says no more than that this reader has nothing to see. There is NO risk column beside it, and that is deliberate rather than missing. A column is declared once for every reader, so a reader without the permission would get a header with nothing under it, which tells them an assessment exists and is most of what the permission was for. The column lands when the list can drop one per reader.

quickFilters.label: Handed on
quickFilters._note: handing-a-case-over REQ-HAND-02. A case moves to the receiving team the moment it is handed, so the sending team's own lens stops answering for it: `assignedGroup` is already Toezicht. `handoverPending` is what keeps it findable while nobody has picked it up, which is the whole failure this lens exists for. It is a projection of the open casetransfer record and never a second custody trail; the trail itself is on the transfer.

quickFilters.label: Archived
quickFilters._note: archived-cases-leave-the-lenses REQ-CM-42, D-3. The ONE lens that asks for archived cases, and a chip rather than a menu entry (ADR-097). `_archived` is openregister's own lens over the archive marker, resolved INSIDE the query the way `_unread` and `_favourite` are, so the page, the total and the facets cannot disagree: absent or false is the working set, `true` is the archive alone and `any` is both. 🔴 NO OTHER LENS ON THIS PAGE CARRIES AN ARCHIVE FILTER, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The platform EXCLUDES archived objects by default from the object list, the aggregation endpoint and every search provider, so a working lens that spelled the exclusion out would be a second copy of a rule that already holds, and the day the two spellings drift the page and the tile beside it disagree. It deliberately carries no `statusHiddenInLists` either, for the reason Closed does not: an archived case is in a terminal status and mostly a hidden one, so filtering here would empty the one list that is supposed to hold them.

quickFilters.label: Closed with no result
quickFilters._note: case-search-declares-its-fields REQ-CSD-04. The register's own example for the missing-value facet: "twelve cases have no result type" is a data quality report nobody has to write. `result_isnull=true` is openregister's declared null grammar (MagicSearchHandler::COMPARISON_OPERATORS), answered server-side, so this is one query and not a page of twenty-five filtered after the fact. A LENS AND NOT A FACET CHIP: a terms facet now carries facet.missing.results, and normalizeFacets() in nextcloud-vue rebuilds the facet from `buckets` alone and drops it, so the count never reaches a consumer (ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue#1176). Reading the raw facet payload beside the normalised one, per app, is the drift the shared normaliser exists to remove. This lens needs no facet payload at all. Deliberately NOT folded into Closed: a closed case with its result recorded is finished work, and burying the ones without it is what lets a year of them pile up unnoticed.

quickFilters.label: My drafts
quickFilters._note: lifecycle-acts-on-the-case REQ-LIFE-14. A draft binds no statutory term and belongs in no working list, so every other lens excludes it and this one is the only way back to it. Scoped to `@me` because a draft is its author's: the case is created assigned to them and dossiq's own case endpoints go through CaseAccessGuard, which grants a case to its assignee and denies everyone else. The per-object grant inside OpenRegister is NOT part of this change, so a reader who queries OpenRegister directly with a filter naming drafts can still see one. Named here rather than implied to be done.

quickFilters.label: With drafts
quickFilters._note: staff-lists-show-drafts-on-request REQ-CM-79, decision 201. The ONE lens that asks for drafts beside the working set. A reader's own drafts are in every list already; this chip adds the drafts of colleagues the reader may read. A draft is the case itself in the status draft (decision 180), and OpenRegister leaves drafts out of every list, count and search unless the query asks: `_drafts` absent is the work list, `true` is drafts alone and `any` is both, resolved inside the query the way `_archived` is. So no other lens spells the exclusion out, and this chip is the filter that shows them. `any` and not `true`, because the question a handler has is 'what is on its way to my list', and that reads in place among the open cases. It carries no `isDraft` condition: that field is dossiq's older draft marker, which My drafts reads, and a case that carries it is a draft too. The lens widens what the list shows, never what the reader may read: a draft stays with its owner unless the schema lets colleagues see drafts.

quickFilters.label: Awaiting payment
quickFilters._note: fees-and-payments-on-the-case REQ-FEE-02. The lens for the money, narrowing on the projection rather than post-filtering a page of twenty-five, so the count and the facets agree with the list. It deliberately does NOT include `stale`: a case whose state could not be read is not a case that owes money, and folding the two would put every case on the instance in this chip the hour shillinq is restarted.

quickFilters.label: Stuck
quickFilters._note: what-a-status-declares, task 3.2. A lens of its own, deliberately NOT folded into Overdue: a case can breach its status maximum while its statutory term is comfortable, and merging the two would bury exactly the case this lens exists to surface. It narrows on `statusDwellBreached`, which the engine writes on the case, so the page, the total and the facets are resolved by one query rather than by a post-filter over a page of twenty-five. A case in a status that declares no maximum can never carry the flag, so on a fleet that has annotated nothing this lens is simply empty.

quickFilters.label: Suspended
quickFilters._note: DqZaken "Opgeschort": the open cases whose term stands still. A pause under Awb 4:5 is not on the case: it is the `status: paused` of the case's term row (`deadlineInstance`, written by DeadlinePauseService), so the lens asks OpenRegister for the case through the term rows that point at it (`_related`, query-related-schema-rows), the way the organisations list asks for its open cases. The case's lifecycle journal says the same, but a JSON string is nothing a list can narrow on.

config._quickFilterMaxVisibleNote: Seventeen pills wrap the actions bar onto a second line and squeeze the 'Showing X of Y' count onto two, so only the first four render and the rest sit behind one more CHIP at the end of the row — a '⋯' pill, not a toolbar button, because what it opens is a filter like the ones beside it. The four are the everyday ones and the cap is the reason the ORDER of quickFilters is now load-bearing: moving a lens up or down moves it in or out of the strip. A lens picked from the panel is applied exactly as a pill is, and the chip then wears its label and its fill, so a narrowed list never presents itself as All.

columns.label: Requester
columns._note: contacts-domain 3.6. The requester is a person OR an organisation, and the two have separate detail pages, so the column needs a route chosen per row. `routeField` + `routeMap` on the built-in `link` cell widget (nextcloud-vue 2.47) read `initiatorType` off the row and pick the page; `params` maps the route's `:id` to the case's `requester` uuid. `contact` is deliberately absent from the map: a Nextcloud contact is not a register row and has no detail page here, so such a row falls back to plain text, which is what InitiatorSection.contactRouteBase() already returns null for. An app-side cell widget in src/cellWidgets.js could branch too, and was rejected: it would reimplement in dossiq the seam every fleet app needs.

columns.label: Status
columns._note: The Status column reads the status's own colour. `statusTypeName` resolves the $ref to the status name, and the library `badge` with `resolve` reads the referenced status type's `colour` (an NL Design System hue) and draws the pill in that hue's tone, so five different statuses never read as one grey column. The name is always the text; the colour only repeats it.

columns.label: Priority

titleWhen.text: Priority set by hand, not derived

columns._note: Keyed on `priorityOrder`, not on `priority`, and that is not a typo. CnDataTable sorts on the server, on the stored value of the column's key, and the stored value of `priority` is a word: sorting by it gives high, low, normal, urgent, which is neither the order a handler means nor a usable one. `priorityOrder` is the order the schema declares (x-enum-order on the priority property) written as an integer by the derivation, so the server sorts it right, and `valueField: priority` makes the cell show the word with its translated `x-enum-labels` label. The pill tone comes from `colorMap`, and a priority set by hand carries a tooltip saying so. The priority FACET in the sidebar is unaffected: it comes from `facetable: true` on `priority` itself, which this change did not touch.

columns.label: Deadline
columns._note: one-case-list A22. A raw ISO date makes every reader do the same subtraction once per row and get it wrong on the rows that matter. The library's `date` cell with `due` renders the days left, "Due today" on the last day and, from the day after, the days overdue in the error colour, with the full date as the tooltip; a case without a deadline shows the library's dash. The column stays sortable: CnDataTable sorts on the stored `deadline`, not on the rendered text.

columns.label: Days in status
columns._note: what-a-status-declares, task 4.2. The number is HELD on the case (currentStatusDwellDays), written by the transition engine as the status changes, which is what makes this column sortable at all: CnDataTable orders on the server, and the process mining page's own dwell figure is reconstructed per request from the statusRecord chain and exists in no column. The library `number` cell reads it in working days and, when `statusDwellBreached` holds, adds a warning chip saying 'stuck' (text, not colour alone). Breached is its own flag and it is NOT the deadline: a case can be stuck for nine weeks inside a term that runs for six months, which is the case this column exists to find. An empty value is an empty cell, never 0.

columns.label: Payment
columns._note: fees-and-payments-on-the-case REQ-FEE-02: whether the leges were paid, on the list as well as on the case, so a teamleider can see which of four hundred aanvragen is waiting on money without opening any of them. It reads the PROJECTION, refreshed hourly by PaymentStateProjectionJob, and that is the whole reason the projection exists: a column cannot ask shillinq once per row. `stale` is a value a reader will see, and it means shillinq could not be asked rather than that the money is late; the gate that refuses acts reads shillinq live and never this column.

columns.label: Decision date
columns._note: columns-follow-the-case-type, row 11.9. The two columns below this line are on the page so a CASE TYPE can ask for them. A scope selects from the page's declared set and cannot add to it, so a case type naming a column the page does not carry has that column dropped in silence, which reads as a case type whose own columns did not take. They sit at the end because the All cases folder shows the page's list in order, and a permit's decision date is not a column a complaint's reader wants third. A THIRD, `riskLevel`, was declared here and is removed: markers-and-assessments-on-the-case refuses a risk column on this list, and the _note on the risk chip above says why. A column is declared once for every reader, so a reader without `dossiq-risk-assessment` would get a header with nothing under it, which tells them an assessment exists and is most of what the permission was for. It lands when the list can drop a column per reader, which nothing in the stack does today.

config._transitionsNote: THE TRANSITION BUTTONS ARE GONE, AND MOVING THE CASE IS NOW A CLICK ON A STAGE. Ruben ruled on 2026-09-12: drop the transition strip and make clicking a status in the timeline widget set that status. So `actionsComponent` no longer names CaseTransitionsWidget, that component is deleted, and the `case-stages` widget carries the gesture. It is the same guarded move it always was, asked for in the same place it is shown: the widget reads OpenRegister /available-actions, dossiq answers that through CaseActionProvider off its own transition engine, and a stage no action reaches is disabled by construction rather than by a check somebody has to remember to write. The strip has been in three places now, and this is the reasoning that survived all three: the status belongs with the status, and the move belongs with the status too. Two things the strip carried have no home on this page any more, and they are named in the page `_note` rather than dropped in silence.
config._breadcrumbsNote: REMOVED, deliberately. The case page carried a trail whose LAST crumb was the case title, rendered one line below the page header that already printed that title: 'Cases > Dakkapel Kerkstraat 12' directly under 'Dakkapel Kerkstraat 12'. It read as a repeat rather than as a location, and it cost the top of the page a row. The way back to the list is the app menu, which is where the other detail pages in this app put it. This key stays as a note and not as config so the next reader finds out the trail was removed on purpose rather than re-adding it.
config._subtitleNote: Placement row A01: the case page did not say which case you are on. `identifier` is the case number, and it reads under the title. THE KEY IS INERT AND STAYS DECLARED ANYWAY. In @conduction/nextcloud-vue 2.49 `subtitleField` is read by CnObjectRow, CnIndexPage and CnObjectList and by no detail-page code at all, so deleting it would change nothing on screen and re-adding it later would look like a new idea. The number reads on the page because `case-tile-number` prints it, which is the same place CaseHeaderRow printed it.
config._note: CASE archetype (unified zaak) — the flagship record and the ADR-062 reference page (the cell is the budget: every widget fills its gridHeight exactly, no inner scrollbars, no reserved voids). The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Core case data' widget (include: identity/ownership fields) with a right column of KPI stats-block (open tasks / documents / decisions / sub-cases, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates) over the Related panel. Row two pairs the 'Process' data widget (include: status/procedure/workflow fields) with Initiator, Contacts and Notes sized to their small content. FK-scoped child collections (task.case, caseDocument.case, decision.case, location.case) fit their rows to their cells with View-all/+N-more footers. Files and Calendar leaves close the page. THE TOP ROW IS FIVE CONFIGURED LIBRARY TILES AND NOTHING SPANS IT. It was one custom component, `case-header`, twelve columns wide and two rows tall, and Ruben's 2026-09-12 ruling is that the widgets on top of the page should be actual KPI widgets configured to show what they show, not a custom widget spanning an entire row. So the band is `case-tile-number`, `case-tile-type`, `case-tile-status`, `case-tile-assignee` and `case-tile-deadline`: four `stat` tiles and one `countdown` tile, all resolved by the library from `content`, none of them a registry component. The widths are 2, 3, 3, 2 and 2, because a case type title and a status name are phrases and a case number, a user id and a countdown are not. Under them the case's own progress is `case-stages`, the library `stages` widget, which is where the case is moved now. `lifecycleActions` is GONE -- it declared `{field: status}` and rendered nothing, because OpenRegister answers no actions for a $ref status field. Suspend, Resume, Extend term and Reopen are ONE `open-modal` header action, `case-lifecycle-menu`, onto CaseLifecycleMenuDialog. This sentence used to name four header actions onto CaseLifecycleActionDialog and there were none: that dialog is retired in retire-the-dead-dialogs, and a stale note is how it stayed hidden. Only Reopen gates exactly as the spec words it, because `isFinalStatus` is on the case record: an action's local `visibleWhen` dot-paths into the loaded record, `suspensionAllowed` and `extensionAllowed` live on the case TYPE, and OpenRegister's object list IGNORES an `id` filter (it answers with the whole table), so a `source` predicate on the type would compare a different case type's flag and be wrong without saying so. Suspension is derived from the case's `activity` journal rather than a flag, so no field can gate Resume either, and that is the one thing this page lost when the transition strip went. The strip carried a Suspended marker and a second Resume button, both driven by GET /api/case/{id}/lifecycle. THE GESTURE STILL HAS A HOME, in the menu: CaseLifecycleMenuDialog reads /available-transitions, /lifecycle and /acts before it offers anything, so a Resume on a case that is not suspended is shown disabled with the server's own sentence rather than silently accepted. There is no `case-resume` header action and there has not been one since the menu landed. THE MARKER DOES NOT. A `stat` tile's `overrides` test the LOADED RECORD, and no property of the case says it is suspended, so there is nothing for a configured tile to bind. Giving it one means materialising a suspension flag on the case, which is its own change: a flag written only on the next suspend would under-report every case suspended before it, and a wrong answer nobody can see is worse than a missing tile. Audit history IS the single sidebar history tab: the `version-history` tab is gone from this page (change case-stages, row A05), and the body strip carries no Timeline entry, so one log lives in one place. Copy case, Start and Plan follow-up (case-actions-menu, rows A24 to A26) are three more `open-modal` header actions, and NOT the `handler` type the design named: a handler action resolves `action.handler` against `effectiveManifest.actions`, which is a JSON map in this file and so cannot hold a function, and dossiq declares no such key, so the entry would warn to the console and do nothing when clicked. The id is `copy-case` and not `copy` because `copy` is one of the five reserved ids CnActionsBar drops at render time to avoid shadowing its built-in. None of the three passes props: open-modal forwards props verbatim without resolving tokens, so `@objectId` would arrive as that literal string, and each dialog reads the route instead. Start gates on `hasStartableFlows`, a materialised boolean on the CASE, exactly as `case-reopen` gates on `isFinalStatus` and for the same reason: a local visibleWhen dot-paths into the loaded case record, `startableFlows` lives on the case TYPE, and OpenRegister ignores an `id` filter so a `source` predicate on the type would compare a different case type's list and be wrong without saying so. An `endpoint` predicate cannot help either, because the URL is fetched verbatim with no token resolution and so cannot name this case.
config._lifecycleMenuNote: lifecycle-acts-on-the-case REQ-LIFE-10. ONE menu, replacing the four header actions that stood here: Suspend, Resume, Extend term and Reopen. They were not wrong, they were SCATTERED: the same case also carried its transitions in the stages widget and its delete behind a third control, each gated differently, so a handler found out what they could do by trying. The dialog merges /available-transitions, /lifecycle and /acts and derives nothing. The entry carries NO visibleWhen, and that is the point of the change: an act the case or the handler's role refuses is shown DISABLED with the reason, never hidden, because the reason is what tells them who to ask. A visibleWhen here could only read the case RECORD anyway, which is why Suspend used to be offered on cases whose TYPE forbids it. The note lives on the page config and not on the action, because a headerAction is a CLOSED object in the manifest schema and rejects an extra key, which is how a first attempt at this note was caught.

widgets.title: Terms and payment
widgets._note: The statutory block: what the law gives you for this case, and what happens to the file afterwards. Every field here already existed on the schema and every one of them carried `visible: false`, which drops a property from every schema-driven surface at once, so the fields were declared and unreadable rather than merely unplaced. `statutoryTerm` is the type's processing deadline copied onto the case: the design asked for `extend` plus the include path `caseType.processingDeadline`, but a data widget builds its fields from the schema's OWN properties, so a dotted include matches nothing and renders nothing, and the stat-caption fallback interpolates only an endpoint payload. `hideEmpty` stays off on purpose: a case with no statutory term must show the row empty, because an absent term is itself the thing a handler is looking for. THE ARCHIVAL HALF MOVED OUT of this widget and no longer has a card of its own. `archiveNomination`, `archiveActionDate` and `archiveStatus` are still written on the case for its ZGW consumers, but they are read from `@self._retention`, the one place any app can ask an object what happens to it and when, and they surface in the object metadata panel under its Archiving category alongside every other `@self` fact. A data widget cannot bind that, because it builds its fields from the schema's own properties and reads them off the top level of the record. The separate `case-archival` card that briefly held them is gone: it duplicated a category the metadata panel already groups, and it spent five rows of the right column saying what the panel says in five.

widgets.title: Hours booked
widgets._note: Hours live in humaniq, per ADR-107 decision 6: 'Hours logged on a case are hrmq time entries carrying the case reference.' So humaniq renders them. This widget is a PLACEMENT of humaniq's `humaniq-hours` leaf, not a query against another app's register. It used to be a stats-block that summed `humaniq`/`TimeEntry` straight out of this manifest, filtered on `domainObjectType` and `domainObjectRef`. On an install without humaniq that endpoint 404s and the tile renders `0`, which is exactly what a case with no hours booked renders: no error, no empty state, nothing a reader would notice. ADR-113 names that class. A leaf whose app is absent is never registered, so the surface goes missing rather than lying. The leaf identifies the host object the way humaniq stores it: `domainObjectType` is the `<app>:<schema>` literal and `domainObjectRef` is the object uuid. Nothing here declares either one. The host forwards `register`, `schema` and `objectId` to every leaf it mounts, and this page's config carries `dossiq` and `case`, so the literal comes out `dossiq:case`. `requiredApp: humaniq` went with the query. It was the honest form of the tile while the tile still read another app's register, and no other integration widget in this manifest declares one. The `log-hours` header action went with it. It wrote a TimeEntry through `open-form`, which the leaf's own Book hours dialog now does, seeded from the same object and beside the total those hours land in. Two booking paths on one page is one more than a reader needs, and the header one was the further from the figure it changes.

widgets.title: Financial documents
widgets._note: financial-documents-on-any-object (Ruben 23 Oct: one Financial documents card). shillinq-financial-documents-panel lists every quote, invoice, credit note, payment request and payout linked to the case and offers issue invoice, request payment, send payment link and record payment, each behind its own shillinq grant; it replaces shillinq-payment-requests-panel, whose acts it keeps. Earlier, fees-and-payments-on-the-case D-1 and D-3: The money lives in shillinq, so shillinq renders it: this is a PLACEMENT of the `shillinq-payment-requests-panel` leaf, the same shape as the humaniq hours leaf beside it, and not a query against another app's register. What the panel shows is the requests raised on this case, the amount, and the article of the legesverordening the amount rests on, because a citizen may ask why they are being charged and "because the configuration says so" is not an answer a gemeente may give. It also carries the acts: raise the leges for this case's intake channel, send the payment link, and record money that arrived another way. THE COUNTER PAYMENT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A DOSSIQ ACT. shillinq puts it behind its own `payment.administer` permission, so the authority that owns the money decides who may say it arrived; a second dossiq path to the same fact would be a second answer with a second rights matrix behind it. dossiq's own half is the word on the case (`paymentState`), refreshed hourly for the list and read live whenever an act must be refused or allowed. A leaf whose app is absent is never registered, so on an install without shillinq this panel is missing rather than empty.

widgets.title: Contract
widgets._note: fees-and-payments-on-the-case D-5. The case names the contract it is handled under and reads its term, its counterparty and what is left of its value from shillinq, which flags a contract that is expiring, expired or terminated because those change what the handler should do next. NOTHING OF THE CONTRACT IS COPIED ONTO THE CASE: a copied term goes stale and then alerts on the wrong date, and the alert before a contract lapses is shillinq's anyway. The case carries one field, `contract`, which is the reference; the other direction is shillinq's `linkedObjects`, which is how a contract lists the cases raised under it.

widgets.title: Flow runs
widgets._note: case-flow-human-steps 6.1, the case half: this case's own flow run and the step it sits on, with its finished runs underneath (nextcloud-vue CnFlowRunsWidget in subject mode). `subject: '@objectId'` binds the current case, so OpenRegister filters the active and completed reads to it server-side. `rowRoute` and not `runRoute` on purpose: dossiq has no run detail page, and FlowDetail (/flows/:id) resolves a FLOW id, so a click opens the flow. Pointing runRoute at FlowDetail would push a run uuid into a flow route and open nothing. The row click also carries the clicked run as `?run=`, so FlowDetail opens with that run inspected and the canvas showing the graph version the run actually executed, rather than the flow's current graph with no run selected. Nothing here declares that: the widget adds the query, and CnPageRenderer forwards `run` to a flow page because that page type declares it reads it.
widgets._pollNote: ⚠️ `pollSeconds: 0` AND NOT THE KEY DELETED, which is the difference between removing a poll and appearing to. CnFlowRunsWidget's `pollMs()` reads `content.pollSeconds` and falls back to 15 when it is undefined or null, so deleting the line leaves the page polling every fifteen seconds while the manifest says nothing about it. `0` is the widget's own documented opt-out and the only spelling that actually stops the timer. WHAT THAT COSTS, stated rather than discovered: a flow run is NOT an OpenRegister object (the engine keeps its runs in its own table behind /apps/openregister/api/flow-runs), so notify_push emits nothing for one and the case's live subscription cannot cover this list. A run advancing usually writes the CASE as well, and that the subscription does catch, so the header and the panels follow it; the runs list itself now refreshes when the widget mounts. Making it live is openregister emitting for a run plus nextcloud-vue refetching on the hint, and a fifteen-second timer on one page was never that.

widgets._note: Placement row A01, first tile, and the one that answers REQ-CDV-14 in practice. widgets.title: Deadline
widgets._note: Placement row A01, fifth tile. The library `countdown` widget TYPE, and deliberately not `stat` with `display: countdown`, which 2.50 also offers and which would make the row five tiles of one type. Three reasons, and the first is the one that decided it. THE WORDINGS WOULD LAND ON THE WRONG CATALOGUE. `CnStatWidget` runs every string through the host's translate function, which this app binds to `ncT('dossiq', key)` in App.vue, so `1 day left`, `{n} days left`, `Today` and `Overdue by {n} days` would become dossiq strings that no gate checks: gate 102 reads manifest strings only, and `check:l10n-js` compares nl.json to nl.js, so a string missing from both is reported in sync. They would render English to a Dutch user and nothing would say so. The `countdown` widget translates them against nextcloud-vue's own catalogue instead, with nothing for this app to maintain. Second, it keeps the absolute date under the headline, which `caption` cannot carry because caption tokens interpolate only from an endpoint payload and this tile is in record mode. Third, configuring `futureLabel` and `pastLabel` to dodge the first reason costs the singular: a configured template replaces both forms, so a case one day out would read `1 days left`. The consistency given up is a type name and a prop name rather than anything a reader sees, because both renderers emit the same `cn-kpi-card` markup from the same stylesheet. It reads a date off the loaded record and does the arithmetic without a request. `thresholds` are the `warn 14, danger 5` bands the retired Time left tile counted with and CaseHeaderRow carried after it: they follow the handling rhythm rather than round numbers, because at two weeks a handler still has room to act and at five days they do not. A date in the past reads as overdue rather than as a negative number, and a case with no deadline reads as a dash in no threshold colour, because a case that has claimed no deadline is neither urgent nor on time. `showDate` keeps the absolute date under the headline: how long and when are two questions and a handler asks both.

widgets.title: Timeline
widgets._note: The case's own progress, as the library `stages` widget: placeable, configurable, and the thing a handler clicks to move the case. The id is `case-stages` and NOT `case-timeline`, which is reserved: `tests/vitest/manifestCaseTimeline.spec.js` asserts this page declares no widget by that id, because row A05 keeps one history in one place and a body panel over the audit log beside the sidebar History tab would be two views of one log. This widget is not that log. It is where the case is in its process and where it is moved. It replaces the custom CaseStepsWidget, whose note said a `stepper` widget type over a reference field's ordered sibling rows would make this a config declaration and that until nextcloud-vue shipped one the custom widget was the interim. It shipped, and this is the declaration. `stagesEndpoint` reads the case type's BLUEPRINT rather than its own statusType rows: a type that derives its lifecycle from a parent has none of its own, so the plain query said this case type has no statuses about a case type that plainly has four, and /blueprint merges the chain server-side. `@object.caseType` is resolved against the loaded case by the library's shared token grammar, and a token that resolves empty blocks the request instead of fetching a url with a hole in it. `transition: {kind: lifecycle}` is what makes a stage clickable: the widget reads OpenRegister's /available-actions, which dossiq answers through CaseActionProvider off its own transition engine, and posts to /transition. 🔴 THE POST IS REFUSED TODAY, AND NOT BY THIS APP. OpenRegister's provider mode is read-only: `deriveActions()` asks the provider, `applyTransition()` has no provider branch, and `LifecycleActionProviderInterface` declares no `execute()`, so a POST of an action the provider itself published comes back `Transition <action> is not declared on this schema.` and the case stays where it is. openregister#3679. `{kind: field}` is NOT the answer: it writes `status` with nothing validating the move, so a handler could close a case with no result and no guard check, and the whole point of this binding is that OpenRegister re-validates. The declaration stays as it is and this page waits for the write half. A stage no action reaches is disabled with the configured `unreachableReason`, and a stage whose move the engine REFUSES is disabled with the guard's own sentence: CaseActionProvider publishes a refused move with `blocked: true` and the guard's `failureMessage` as its description, and 2.50's `stageAccess()` reads that flag. So the refusal is drawn before the click rather than met after it, and `onStageClick` refuses a blocked move as well, so no path through the widget posts one. Both kinds of refusal fail closed twice over, because OpenRegister still re-validates the POST through the same engine that published the verdict. Vertical: a status name is a phrase, not a word, and laid out left to right those phrases wrap into stacked columns that read as a table rather than as a sequence.

widgets.title: Case panels
widgets._note: Panels describing one case used to be cards stacked down the page, each with its own header and Actions menu, only one of them ever being read. The strip takes over the title and the card, the children render bare, and the Actions menu is hoisted into the bar where it rebinds to whichever tab is open. Every child is DELIBERATELY absent from `layout`: the tabs widget renders them, so a layout entry would render each one twice. THE COUNT IS THE POINT. This strip carried FOURTEEN tabs and now carries TEN: it went to SIX, which is what the placement work asked for, and then Notes (2026-09-12) and Timeline (one-timeline-on-the-case) were each added on a reason recorded in their own entry. Timeline is the one tab here that does NOT own a collection: it reads the entries the tabs beside it write, which is why it adds a tab rather than replacing three. FOUR went because they were already somewhere else on this page: Notes, Mail and Decisions each duplicated a sidebar tab, and the sidebar copy is the better one in at least the Notes case, because CaseNotesTab emits @mention and the body widget predates it. That is the rule the History tab already set on this page: one log in two places is duplication, not coverage. FOUR MORE went by folding, through the `case-sections` container widget, which puts two panels behind one label. That is why Files did not have to be dropped to leave the strip: it keeps the files leaf's share and comment surface as a section of Documents. `case-core` is the only tab that still names one widget. It is the case's own fields, and the raw-data view plan item 2.22 asks for is a SIDEBAR tab over every property, not this surface. It moved IN from the layout grid because reading the case data cost a scroll past the panels that answer the same question. NO TAB ENTRY NEEDS `visibleIf` ANY MORE, and that blocker can be closed rather than waited on. It was wanted so a collection holding nothing could be absent rather than empty. With six tabs each holding two collections, an empty section is a line of text inside a tab a handler opened on purpose, which is not the same failure as a tab that promises content and has none.

widgets.title: Data
widgets._note: The Data tab: the case record, and where it is. The map is a section here rather than a tab of its own because geography is metadata ON the case rather than a collection beside it, and a handler reading the address wants it next to the fields.

widget.title: Core case data
widget._note: `identifier` carries `readOnly: true` in the schema because OpenRegister generates it, and fieldsFromSchema DROPS a readOnly property outright unless an override re-admits it. So the case number sat in this include list and rendered nowhere at all — the very field five of the seven demo cases were reported as missing. The `identifier` override re-admits the field with `readOnly: false` and then keeps it un-editable with `editable: false`, which is the state the requirement asks for: shown, never typed.

widget.title: Priority
widget._note: Where this case's priority came from. `priority` itself sits in Core case data above, shown and never typed; this section is the reasoning behind it. Every field here is `readOnly: true` in the schema except the two a person actually sets, and fieldsFromSchema DROPS a readOnly property outright unless an override re-admits it — the same trap the `identifier` note records one section up — so each carries `readOnly: false` with `editable: false`, which is the state the requirement asks for: shown, never typed. THE TWO EDITABLE FIELDS ARE THE OVERRIDE AND ITS REASON. Setting `priorityOverride` is how a person overrules the matrix; who set it and when are stamped from the session by CasePriorityDerivationListener rather than offered as fields, because whose decision it was is a fact about the edit and not something anybody should be able to type. Clearing the override clears its byline and its reason with it and returns the case to the value the matrix derives now. `hideEmpty` stays off: a case with no override must show the row empty, because the absence is the answer a handler is looking for.

widget.title: Incidents
widget._note: splitting-a-case-and-its-incidents REQ-CM-53. Several dated reports inside one case, which is how repeat reports on one address are handled: the case holds the address and the history, and each report is a record with its own reporter, its own owner and its own outcome. SORTED BY `eventDate` AND NOT BY THE RECORDING MOMENT (D-6): a report written up three weeks late belongs where it happened, and `createdAt` order would quietly rewrite the sequence the case is about. It sits in the Work tab rather than in a tab of its own, because the strip is already eleven entries and an incident is work on the case; `recordedAt` is a column beside the event date so the delay between the two is visible rather than hidden. NOT a deelzaak: an incident has no number, no term and no decision, and making one would give every report a beslistermijn it does not have (D-4).

widget.title: Planned actions
widget._note: task-dependencies-and-the-next-planned-action, gap register row 3.28. A case answers what happens next WITHOUT anybody reading the history, which is the whole reason the record exists. It sits beside Tasks rather than inside it because the two answer different questions: a task is work somebody is doing now, a planned action is work the case type says comes next and that nobody has started. The filter keeps `state: planned` and the sort is `plannedFor` ascending, so the FIRST ROW IS THE ANSWER; completed actions stay readable through the case's own object list rather than crowding the one sentence this section exists to say. `plannedFrom` is a column on purpose: it is what makes a chain readable backwards, so a handler can see that this call was planned by the confirmation before it rather than by somebody typing a date. Rows carry no `rowRoute`: there is no plannedAction detail page, and a route naming a page that does not exist pushes vue-router at a name it cannot resolve.

Task lifecycle belongs to WorkflowEngineService alone and the kanban WorkflowBoardView is the workflow surface; a mirror would give a handler two places to finish the same work and no rule about which one counts. A SECTION of the Work panel rather than a body widget with a layout entry, which is what the design named: the case body is a tab strip and its grid is full, and a card board is work, so it belongs beside the tasks. The leaf owns link, create and unlink, so dossiq ships no Deck code at all; with the Deck app absent the library renders its own empty state rather than an error.

widgets.title: Who else is here
widgets._note: object-presence (openregister#3875, nextcloud-vue#1204 and #1205). Who else has this case open, so two handlers find each other BEFORE they overwrite each other rather than afterwards. It is the softer half of the edit lock beside it: the lock refuses a save, and this makes the refusal unnecessary by making the other person visible while there is still time to talk. 🔴 TYPE IS THE LIBRARY'S OWN WIDGET TYPE AND NOT A REGISTRY KEY, which is why this app ships no component for it. The widget takes its register, schema and object from the SURFACE, so a manifest cannot point presence at a different record from the one on screen, and a bug in it is fixed by one library release rather than by one in each of the twenty-one apps. Silent when nobody else is there, which is almost always, so it costs no vertical space until it has something to say. ⚠️ INERT UNTIL THE LIBRARY SHIPS: `presence` is registered in @conduction/nextcloud-vue on parity/round2 and not in the 3.2.0 this app has installed, so CnDetailWidgetHost resolves it to nothing and renders nothing at all, which is what it does for any unknown type. No error and no empty box; it starts working on the version bump.

widgets.title: Custody
widgets.subtitle: Who has had this case in hand
widgets._note: Who has held this case, and who is asking for it (registry type case-custody-pane -> CaseCustodyPanel). Rendered by TYPE because a tab child resolves from cnRegistry[widget.type]: a page `slots` map is read by the widget GRID and never reaches a widget inside a tab panel, which is how two earlier panels in this app shipped as an empty tab that logged nothing. It sits beside Timeline rather than inside it on purpose: the timeline says what CHANGED and this says who HELD it, and reading a sequence of diffs back into a holding is a reconstruction rather than a record. It is a custom widget and NOT a data widget because a holding is only meaningful as a JOIN, between the moment one holding ended and the moment the next began; a row of values per holding would look complete on a chain with a gap in it.

widgets.title: Archiving
widgets._note: What happens to this case when its business use ends, as openregister decided it (library widget type retention -> CnRetentionWidget). Every value is read off @self._retention and @self.archived, which openregister writes; the widget derives nothing, so a records manager never reads a second derivation that could disagree with the stored one. A case nobody could nominate is drawn apart from a case nobody has closed yet. archiveStatus is the case's own ZGW field, and a disagreement with openregister's archived marker is said out loud. Recomputing asks the archivist for a reason before it sends.

widgets.title: Knowledge
widgets._note: knowledge-base-on-the-case, row 11.26. Two sections, because the row asks two questions that have different answers. The FIRST is the work instruction for this KIND of case, which the case type names once and every case of that type shows without anybody linking anything: that is the whole point of the row, and it is rendered by the `case-work-instruction` type because the value lives on the case TYPE while the page is bound to the CASE, and CnDetailPage reads no `extend`, so a declared widget over a dotted `caseType.knowledgeBasePage` path would render blank while looking configured. The SECOND is the pages somebody linked to THIS case, through OpenRegister's `collectives` leaf. dossiq stores no article text and renders no wiki of its own: Collectives owns the page, its history, its versions and its team, and the team is what makes visibility per role, because a collective is scoped to a Nextcloud team and `roleType.ncGroupId` already names the group behind a role. So a handler who may not read a page in Collectives does not read it through a case either, and there is nothing here to enforce or to leak. TYPE `case-sections` AND NOT TWO TABS: one Knowledge tab that holds both is the reader's question, and CaseSectionsWidget drops the heading of a section whose widget drew nothing, so a case type with no instruction shows the linked pages alone rather than an empty block. The leaf keeps its own `requiredApp: "collectives"`, so on an instance without the app it is never registered and that section goes missing rather than drawing an empty knowledge base. `xwiki` is in `case.linkedTypes` beside it for the municipalities that run one. MEASURED 2026-09-20: the `xwiki` descriptor ships in the library but is NOT in `leafIntegrations[]`, and OpenRegister registers it only from its own `main.js`, not from the always-on `integration-global` bundle, so it does not resolve on a dossiq page and nothing here places it. That is an openregister row, not a reason to declare a widget that can never render.

tabs.label: Audit trail
tabs._note: Placement row A05: ONE history of the case. This tab is the case timeline, CnAuditTrailTab over OpenRegister's audit trail for this object, newest first, with the actor and the action on every row. The `version-history` tab that sat beside it is GONE from THIS page: it read the same audit rows as a field diff, which is what made the case show its history twice and neither of them well. The other 13 detail pages keep theirs, and the `VersionHistoryLeafTab` registry entry stays because they resolve it; row A05 scores the case page only. Three things this tab still cannot do, each a need rather than a defect: it cannot OPEN on writes, because `actionFilter` is internal state on CnAuditTrailTab and this widget declares only `register`, `schema`, `objectId`, `title` and `maxDisplay`; it cannot EXPORT, because the tab has no export action; and it cannot carry document, note and mail events beside the audit rows, because a merged per-object feed is the OpenRegister `activity` leaf, which does not exist. Until each lands the tab opens unfiltered over writes and reads, with the Action and User filters it already renders. There is deliberately NO body tab over the same log: the tab strip carries no Timeline entry, because one log in two places is the duplication this row retires. The `case-stages` widget on the grid is not that log: it is where the case is in its process and where a handler moves it, not what has happened to it.

tabs.label: Terms
tabs._note: phase-terms-and-the-internal-target REQ-TERM-060 to REQ-TERM-068: the four clocks on this case, each apart. A gemeente runs the statutory term the applicant was told about, the planned end the team steers on, the internal target a teamleider steers on, and the phase term inside the case term. Collapsing them into one field made a case that is on time for the citizen and six weeks late for the team read green. A `component:` tab and not a `widgets[]` one, for the reason the Access tab gives: a sidebar tab renders either a registered component or a CnObjectSidebar built-in (data, metadata, audit / audit-trail, object-table), and none of the four can read /api/cases/{id}/terms. The progress figure and the days-left count are the SERVER'S, computed at read time and stored nowhere, so the list column reads the same computation when the library carries a column type for it.
