A `component:` tab and not a `widgets[]` one, because a sidebar tab renders either a registered component or a CnObjectSidebar built-in (data, metadata, audit / audit-trail, object-table), and none of the four can read OpenRegister's permission catalogue, role definitions or deny preview. dossiq computes no effective permission here: the panel renders what OpenRegister answered, one row per rule.

tabs.label: AVG
tabs._note: data-subject-requests-drive-the-platform REQ-AVG-DSR-01: what OpenRegister reported about this case's data subject, and the acts dossiq drives on it. Declared on every case rather than only on a data subject request, because a sidebar tab list is one declaration on the case page and gating it on a field would need a per-case condition the host does not evaluate here. The panel reads the request kind itself and shows the erasure half, the export half, or an empty state saying this case is not a data subject request; the empty state is what stops one platform request per case opened. A `component:` tab and not a `widgets[]` one, because none of CnObjectSidebar's built-ins can call the AVG endpoints or render a protected item with its ground and its remedy.

tabs.label: Tags
tabs._note: A sidebar tab renders EITHER a registered `component` or `widgets[]` whose `type` is a CnObjectSidebar built-in (data, metadata, audit / audit-trail, object-table). A `type: "custom"` entry here resolves to nothing and renders an empty panel with a console warning nobody reads — the page-slot mechanism (`widget-<id>`) only applies to layout grid items. So this is the `data` built-in over the single `tags` field: it is handed the loaded case and the resolved schema by the host, and an array-of-strings property already resolves to the tags editor. The `widget` override says so out loud, so a later change to the type cannot silently turn the editor into a text box.

config._linkObjectNote: `case` is REQUIRED on the caseObject schema and is deliberately absent from `link-object`'s `includeFields`: an `open-form` action saves straight to the object API, so a required property the form does not ask has to arrive through `props` or the save is refused with a validation error the handler cannot act on. `@objectId` is the open case, the same shape `add-party` and `log-contact` use. Until nextcloud-vue passes `props` into the create form as initial data (triage #6) the field is not prefilled on screen; the value is still written, which is what the e2e asserts.
config._inspectNote: admin-inspect-entry row 2.22. TWO FLAT ACTIONS, NOT ONE WITH CHILDREN, which is what the design asked for. CnDetailPage runs CnActionButtons in `display: "menu"`, and that mode renders no buttons of its own: it emits `menuEntries`, which maps the visible actions into menu descriptors and drops `children` on the floor. A parent with two children would therefore have shown ONE menu item and neither entry, with no warning anywhere. The chevron the `children` key documents only ever renders in the inline `barActions` mode, which a detail page never uses. The design also named `adminOnly`; there is no such key. A manifest action is a CLOSED object in the nextcloud-vue schema and its vocabulary has no admin flag, and of visibleWhen's three modes only `endpoint` can ask about the READER: the local mode dot-paths into the case record and the source mode queries OpenRegister objects, and neither knows who is looking. So both actions carry the same gate, GET /api/inspect/availability, and evaluation is fail-safe, which means a broken predicate hides them rather than showing them to everyone. Hiding is an AFFORDANCE and not a control: both surfaces read through OpenRegister, which refuses a non-admin itself. Raw data opens `CaseRawDataDialog` and NOT `CnObjectMetadataModal`, which the design named: that component takes a required `objectData` object an open-modal action cannot hand it, and it renders the `@self` block rather than the record, so it would have opened on a case and shown no stored property at all.
config._editLockNote: edit-lock-on-the-case-page REQ-CM-39, row 2.27. Two caseworkers silently overwriting each other was, in the gap register's own words, a real failure mode we had no answer to. The answer is the PLATFORM lock, and the take, the release and both displays belong to CnDetailPage rather than to this manifest: opening the edit form acquires, closing it and a successful save release, leaving the page releases through the composable's scope, and Edit is withdrawn while another user holds it rather than offered and then refused by the write. Nothing here declares any of that, and nothing should: a key that turned the lock on per page would be a second answer to a question one detail page answers for every app in the fleet. 🔴 WHAT THIS PAGE OWES THE LOCK IS TWO STRINGS. The lock url is built from `config.register` and `config.schema`, and a slug no register answers to comes back 404, at which point the acquire fails for a reason that is not a conflict, the form stays open on purpose and the edit proceeds with NO LOCK AT ALL, silently. That is not hypothetical: nextcloud-vue passed the object-cache key `<register>-<schema>` into that url until #1202, and the release sent a DELETE to a route OpenRegister does not declare and read its own 404 as success, so no lock was ever taken or handed back on any manifest-driven detail page. `tests/vitest/caseEditLock.spec.js` is what keeps the pair honest here. ⚠️ A HELD LOCK DOES NOT YET REFUSE A SAVE: openregister `run-scoped-object-locking` is unshipped, so today the lock is what the second handler is SHOWN, and the write guard arrives with that change.
config._archivedNote: archived-cases-leave-the-lenses REQ-CM-43, D-4. Seven header actions that WRITE to the case are gated on `@self.archived`, the platform's own marker, read straight off the case object the page already holds: the LOCAL form of `visibleWhen` dot-paths into that object, so the gate costs no round trip. `empty` is how absence is spelled. It used to be `eq null`, and that hid all seven on every case that was NOT archived: OpenRegister leaves the `archived` key off `@self` until a case is archived, so the read is undefined, and `eq` holds only for null itself or for the word "null". `empty` holds for undefined, null and the empty string, and a present marker is an object, which is never empty. THE FOUR THAT ARE NOT GATED ARE DELIBERATE. Claim, Release and Hand to another team already carry `isFinalStatus neq true`, and a case can only be archived once it has ended, so they are already gone on an archived case; `visibleWhen` holds ONE condition and no AND, so adding the archive to them would mean dropping the condition doing the work. Copy case stays, because a copy is a NEW case and writes nothing to this one. The Lifecycle menu stays, because Restore lives inside it and gating it would hide the one act that undoes the archive. Start keeps its own `hasStartableFlows` gate for the same one-condition reason, and a flow that writes to an archived case is refused by OpenRegister with a sentence naming the archive. 🔴 THE GENERIC EDIT BUTTON IS STILL OFFERED, AND DOSSIQ CANNOT TAKE IT AWAY PER RECORD. `config.showEditAction` is a page-level boolean in the manifest schema and CnDetailPage has no predicate form of it, so pressing Edit opens the form, saving is refused by the platform, and the refusal names the archive, the archiving user and the date. That is the reason reaching the reader rather than a silent failure, but it arrives after the click where the other six are simply not there. It belongs in nextcloud-vue, where one detail page reading `@self.archived` answers for every app in the fleet.
config._claimNote: Claim and Release (case-claim-action, row 2.4). Both are `api-call` header actions and NOT the `handler` type the change's design named: a handler header action resolves `action.handler` against `effectiveManifest.actions`, a JSON map in this file, so it cannot hold a function and the entry would warn to the console and do nothing when clicked. That is the same finding the copy-case sentence records. BOTH ARE NOW GATED ON THE ASSIGNEE, which needed vocabulary that did not exist: a local `visibleWhen` compared one dot-path against one literal, with no way to ask whether a field is empty, no resolution of `@me` in `value`, and no way to require two facts at once. nextcloud-vue 2.39.0 adds `empty`/`notEmpty`, resolves `value` through the shared @-token grammar, and composes with `all`/`any`. So Claim shows only where CaseAssignmentService::claim() would accept it (nobody holds the case) and Release only where release() would (the reader holds it), and the two can no longer be offered together. The SERVER still refuses either with a 409 and a sentence, which is the backstop rather than the gate. Neither action sets `errorMessage`, on purpose: the library shows its own text when one is set and the server's sentence when it is not, and the server's sentence is the one that says why.
config._crossDomainNote: the-social-domain-plan-and-its-grounds REQ-XDV-01 and REQ-XDV-02, row 5.18. Whether an open case exists in another social-domain register, which one, and who to call. Three facts, and there is no show-more: purpose limitation between Wmo, Jeugdwet and Participatiewet does not allow the 360 view row 5.4 asks for, and every field beyond those three is one somebody has to justify. A modal rather than an api-call because the GROUND is the act and is chosen BEFORE the answer: a ground filled in afterwards is a formality, and choosing it first is what makes the log mean something when the person asks what was looked up about them. Not gated on a group here, deliberately: the guard is that a ground has been chosen, the service refuses without one before it reads anything, and it writes the ground, the person, the requester, the moment and what came back to `sociaalDomeinAuditLog` in the same act as the answer, which is the field that had been declared and unread since the register was written.
config._rebindNote: case-rebind (case-type-rebind): move a running case to a DIFFERENT case type, which the version move beside it refuses by design. A case filed under the wrong type used to be closed and refiled, with a new number, a new term and a paper trail that stops; a rebind keeps all three. It is a modal because the MAPPING is the act: across two case types a status name means nothing, so the landing status is asked for and so is every property the target requires in that status. The action is gated on `visibleWhen` rather than on a group key, because an action carries no group vocabulary: the endpoint answers whether the caller is a case coordinator, and the service checks the same group itself, since a hidden button is not an authorization.
config._versionMoveNote: case-version-move (case-type-version-chain): move this case to another version of its OWN case type, which nothing could do. A case filed the day before a correction was published had to be closed and refiled under a new number. It is a modal and not a confirm-gated api-call because the PREVIEW is the act's substance: the person moving the case is shown the status it lands in, the statuses and fields the other version adds and drops, and which of the dropped fields this case has already answered. Every one of those, and the refusal when the other version has no status by the name this case is sitting in, comes from the server, so the dialog cannot disagree with the write. Moving a case to a DIFFERENT case type is a rebind and is not this act: `case-type-rebind` owns that and declares this change as its dependency. Hidden on a closed case, like the other acts that rewrite what governs it.
config._sendDigitalPostNote: digital-post-consumes-integriq, the `send-digital-post` header action. It opens BerichtenboxComposeDialog, which was referenced NOWHERE in dossiq until 2026-09-18: not by src/registry.js, not by this file, not by another component, and the only occurrence of its name in the repository was its own `name:` line. So the compose surface worked, the routing service worked, the message was stored on the case, and nobody could press anything to reach any of it. `open: true` because CnAppRoot mounts a registry modal with the action's props verbatim and the dialog renders on `open`; `caseId` is passed for the same reason BeschikkingComposerDialog's is and is IGNORED while it holds the unresolved `@objectId` token, because open-modal resolves no tokens and the route answers instead. `visibleWhen` tests `initiatorType`, a materialised field on the CASE and therefore readable by a local predicate, exactly as `case-reopen` tests `isFinalStatus`: only a person has a digital post box, and a company case would otherwise offer a gesture whose recipient field can only be filled with a KvK number. It is NOT gated on integriq being installed, and that is deliberate: an instance without integriq refuses the send and names the missing app, which is a sentence a handler can act on, while a button that is simply absent is a capability nobody can ask about.
config._wooPublishNote: woo-publish-decision-from-the-case D-4 and D-11. The Woo header actions replace the removed assessment view's publish and withdraw controls (#867), which no page reached; nothing else on the case page publishes. Publish is offered on a ready case only, so a withdrawn decision is published again through the same route, not from the header. Publish and withdraw show only to the case's assignee (`assignee` eq `@me`): the API (CaseAccessGuard::hasCaseMutationAccess) also lets an admin through, but every gate here is LOCAL on purpose. CnActionButtons evaluates header predicates one after another and renders an action whose predicate has not answered yet, so an `endpoint` condition (the admin probe) leaves Publish on screen for as long as that request is pending, and so does every action listed after an endpoint-gated one. That is why these three sit before case-rebind, the first endpoint-gated action. An admin who does not handle the case claims it first. A hidden button is not an authorization; the endpoint still checks. Publishing asks first, because it makes documents public; the dialog carries the action's label and the library's question, since the manifest schema (2.41.0) has no confirmTitle or confirmMessage though CnActionButtons reads both. Once published, the header carries a link to the publication (`woo-publication-open`), an external `navigate` the action bar renders as an anchor. A refusal shows the server's `message`, which the controller translates.
config._exportDossierNote: document-acts-reach-a-surface REQ-ZAK-022, the `export-dossier` header action. The whole case file as one download, over ZaakdossierDownloadController::downloadZip, which answers a DataDownloadResponse of a zip carrying manifest.csv at its root and one sub-folder per informatieobjecttype (ZipManifestBuilder). `download: true` is the shape that asks for the response as a blob and hands it to the browser; without it an api-call shows a success toast over a zip nobody receives. NOT `/api/dossier/{caseId}/export`, which the change's own tasks named: that route is DossierExportController and it answers a JSON export PLAN for a beroep dossier, not bytes, so an action declared on it would have downloaded a file called dossier.zip holding JSON. Both routes guard on CaseAccessGuard::hasCaseReadAccess and refuse with 403 and no bytes; the plan route had no test for that until this change and has one now. No `visibleWhen`: the export is offered on an open case and on a closed one, because the archive export of a CLOSED case is half of what this action is for. FolderZipOutline was not in src/icons.js and is registered now, because an unregistered name renders no icon at all rather than a fallback glyph (hydra gate-60).

config._sourceNote: remove-casetask 2.2. The list is the ENGINE's task inbox, not OpenRegister objects over a `caseTask` schema, so `register`, `schema` and `extend` are gone rather than left behind as config nothing reads. `rowRoute` is what keeps the page dossiq's: the source's own `openRow` calls window.location.assign on OpenRegister's task page, and a `row-click` listener cannot recover a navigation that has already left the app, which is why nextcloud-vue#1063 added the prop. `columns` is deliberately ABSENT. The source supplies six, with state and priority as badges whose colour maps are built from the same t() calls as their labels, so the lookup holds in every locale; reproducing that here to rename one header would be a divergent copy of the thing this change removes, and if the wording matters it belongs upstream as a label override. TWO VISIBLE DELTAS, both deliberate: the case column's header now reads Subject, and the Team column is gone because the engine models candidate groups as a LIST and has no single assigneeGroup to read.
config._savedViewSaveNote: The board draws no Weergave opslaan in the toolbar; the saved views stay in the side panel.
config._savedViewsNote: Saved views are managed on every index page (Ruben, 20 October 2026): save, apply, edit, share with people and groups, add to the menu under My views, copy a default, delete, all in the sidebar's Filters tab. This page reads the engine's task inbox, not a schema, so its views are scoped to the source by name, the same key nextcloud-vue gives a named-source page by default. A view keeps the sidebar's fields (case, state, priority, kind, due between) and the search term; the lens chips stay chips.
config._quickFiltersNote: one-case-list: the same six lenses the Cases index carries, in the same order and with the same labels, so a person who learned one list has learned the other. Only what sits underneath changed: `isTerminalStatus` was `caseTask`'s materialised boolean and `isTerminal` is the engine's own, and the two due windows are `dueAfter`/`dueBefore` predicates the engine answers (openregister#3581) rather than string comparisons against a `dueDate` column. 🔴 `scope` IS SET EXPLICITLY ON EVERY LENS. The task endpoint defaults to `scope: assigned`, so a lens that left it off would quietly answer 'my closed tasks' where this list has always meant 'closed tasks'. Only Mine and Unclaimed are person-scoped, and they now say so rather than inheriting it. config._note: CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (WMS/WFS map-layer definition). Admin-only, no comms, no child schemas and no status lifecycle — so deliberately lean. The single Data widget holds the full endpoint config (url, layerName, srs, opacity, queryable, format, version, isDefault, active). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a layer), no content leaves (a layer carries no files/notes/calendar), no lifecycleActions (active is a plain boolean). Audit history (config edits) is a sidebar tab.

woo-refusal-grounds-list REQ-WRG-003. The settled grounds of design D-2 (decision 133). Sorted by code with the broader ground beside each, so the list reads as the tree: 5.1, then 5.1.1 and its letters, then 5.1.2 and its letters. Add creates a narrower ground under a parent code; editing the status to retired is how a ground is retired, because WooRefusalGroundDeleteGuard refuses a delete while anything cites it. No board on identity.conduction.nl/screens draws this page.

woo-refusal-grounds-list REQ-WRG-003 and REQ-WRG-004. One ground with its law text and source. The History tab is OpenRegister's audit trail for the object, so every add, edit and retirement shows who, when and the values before and after.

WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (inter-organisation case handover). No comms/documents and no child schemas — a transfer is a small state machine, not a dossier. The single Data widget carries the request and its resolution (caseId, sourceOrganization, targetOrganization, reason, requestedDate, rejectionReason, completedAt), and lifecycleActions drive the status (pending → accepted / rejected). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a transfer), no content leaves. Audit history (the pending→accepted/rejected transition) is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Supplier portal accounts
pages._note: The accounts suppliers hold on the supplier portal. The schema shipped with leverancier-zaakportaal and the page never did, so for three months an instance created the storage, filled it, and offered nobody a way to look at it. That is a privacy problem before it is a usability one: a supplier user is a named person with an email address and an eHerkenning level, and a data subject asking what is held about them could not be answered from this app at all. THE ACTIVATION TOKEN IS NOT A COLUMN, deliberately. It is a one-time credential, it is on the record because the activation flow needs it, and a list is exactly the wrong place for it: an admin screenshotting this page would be handing out account access. The sidebar shows the whole record for anybody who genuinely needs the field, which is one deliberate click rather than a wall of tokens. Admin-only for the same reason the Tenants page is: these are accounts, and the answer to `who may read them` is the same answer as `who may create them`.

config._pageTabsNote: Board DqContracten: Contracts, Suppliers and Portal accounts are one set of tabs. Portal accounts shows only to an admin (the tab is hidden, this page refuses others), so it carries no count on the procurement pages: a hidden tab's count is still requested.

pages.title: Data breach register
pages._note: The datalek register, AVG art. 33. The schema shipped with sociaal-domein-zaaktypes and nothing ever showed it, so an incident could be recorded by an import and read by nobody, and the 72-hour notification clock the schema exists to evidence had no surface at all. The columns are the three facts a supervisor asks for in that hour: when it happened, whether the AP has to be told, and whether it has been. `cause` leads because a register nobody can scan is a register nobody uses. Only for the privacy officers, admin and beheerders (`permission: privacy`, schema block in register.d/92): a breach record names how personal data escaped, which is itself a disclosure.

pages.title: Field evidence
pages._note: What an inspector captured in the field. The schema shipped with mobiel-inspectie-offline and nothing ever read it, so a photo or a voice memo could be uploaded from a device and reach nobody. THE COLUMNS ARE THE ENVELOPE, NOT THE CONTENT. `transcription` is what somebody said, `cloudUrl` is a direct link to the file and `gpsLocation` is where a person stood; none of the three belongs in a list that is scanned rather than opened, and `sensitivityLevel` exists on this schema precisely because the content is classified. So the page shows which inspection, what kind, when, whether the transcription finished and how sensitive it is, and the record itself opens in the sidebar. ADMIN-ONLY IS A PLACEHOLDER, and an honest one: the right reader is the handler working the inspection, and there is no inspection page to hang this off yet. Until there is, the choice is between an operational surface for the people who administer the instance and no surface at all, which is what it had.

pages.title: Offline sync queue
pages._note: The outbox of a device that worked offline. Nothing in dossiq enqueues or drains it yet, so this page will be empty on every instance today, and that is the point: an empty list somebody can look at is how you find out the offline story ends at the schema, where before there was nothing to look at and no way to tell. `payload` is not a column because it is the whole object being replayed; `lastError` is, because a queue that stopped draining is the only thing anybody comes here to find out.

pages.title: Offline sync conflicts
pages._note: Where the device and the server disagreed. The two version snapshots are the record and not the list: comparing them is what the sidebar is for, and a column holding one of them would print an object. `resolution` is nullable until somebody resolves it, so a blank in that column is the queue of work rather than a missing value.

pages.title: Needs assessments
pages._note: The Wmo assessment a consulent writes, and the support it advises. It shipped with sociaal-domein-zaaktypes and nothing ever read it, so an assessment about a named citizen could be recorded and reached by nobody. THE COLUMNS ARE THE FACTS OF THE PROCESS, NOT ITS CONTENT. `advisedSupport` is what somebody is to receive and `investigationMinutes` points at the interview write-up; both are the record and belong in the sidebar, not in a list that is scanned. `dateInvestigation` leads because the Wmo gives six weeks from the application and this is the page that shows whether that was met. Admin-only for now, and the note the other sociaal-domein pages carry applies here too: the right reader is the consulent on the case, and the case page has no panel for this yet.

pages.title: Multidisciplinary consultations
pages._note: The multidisciplinary meeting several cases are discussed in. `toestemmingenGeregistreerd` is a column and the first thing to look at: an MDO where consent was not registered for every participant is data shared about a household that nobody agreed to, and until this page existed there was no way to find one. `minutes` and `gedeeldeGegevens` are deliberately not columns, for the reason the schema itself gives: the minutes are anonymised only WHEN consent is missing, so the unanonymised ones are the sensitive case and a list is the wrong place to meet them. Decidiq owns meetings for the fleet, so whether this record should live here at all is a question this page makes askable rather than answers.

config._note: COMMITTEE archetype (bezwaaradviescommissie / BAC), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves on the schema. A committee is defined by its constitution and its caseload; the schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Committee' (name, type, domain, jurisdiction, quorum, active — the constitution) and 'Roster & term' (chair, secretary, members[], termStartsOn, termEndsOn, created — who sits and until when). The lead row pairs the constitution widget with an in-grid KPI stats-block (total assignments + in-deliberation workload via bacAdviceRequest.status, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). Below: the roster widget full-width, then the advice-assignment object-list (bacAdviceRequest.commissie=@objectId). No status lifecycle (active is a boolean). Audit history (composition/term changes) is a sidebar tab.

config._note: ADVICE-ASSIGNMENT archetype (a committee advice request on a bezwaar), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves and no child schemas. The 15-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Assignment' (who/when — bezwaar, commissie, panel, status, assignedAt, deadline) paired with the Related panel (parent bezwaar and committee), and 'Advice & outcome' (the substantive opinion, dissent and evidence — advice, recommendation, conclusion, adviceIssuedAt, dissentingOpinions[], adviceDocuments, signatureEvidence, hearingReportRef) full-width below. lifecycleActions drive the status (assigned → in-deliberation → advice-issued / niet-ontvankelijk). Document references are plain fields, not a files-leaf. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._dossierExportNote: four-unreachable-surfaces: GET /api/dossier/{caseId}/export answers the Awb-ordered plan BeroepDossierExport builds, and no line of src/ had ever called it. It is NOT CaseDetail's Export dossier, which downloads the whole case file as a zip; this one is the submission ORDER, which is the part a court reads first. An api-call cannot host it, because the route answers JSON and would have handed the reader a file called dossier.zip holding JSON, which is the reason document-acts-reach-a-surface left it alone. So it is an open-modal onto DossierExportPanel, read-only: it renames nothing and writes nothing, and shows what the export would contain so the mistake is found before the submission.
config._note: APPEAL-CASE archetype (AWB beroep at the rechtbank), ADR-062 round 2. `beroep` is a supporting schema on a unified case (beroep.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes, so no files/notes/contacts/calendar here — those live on the parent CaseDetail. The 17-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Appeal' (the court header — case, sourceBezwaar, contestedDecision, courtReference, responsibleChamber, competentCourt) paired with the Related panel (parent case and source bezwaar), and 'Filing & judgment' (the clock, sub-process and outcome — appellantFilingDate/NotifiedDate, filingDeadline, voorzieningRequested, latefilingNotice, fileInspectionRequests[], judgmentOutcome/Date/Document, cascadeAction/cascadeBezwaarCase) full-width below. No status enum on this schema, so no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._formNote: The Add dialog on this page asked all 41 of caseType's properties, in one column, at default dialog width. Nothing was wrong with the dialog: CnFormDialog has taken `size` and `columns` since two-column forms shipped, but CnIndexPage passed neither, so the built-in Add form had no way to ask. The `case` create form on the Dashboard and the two contact pages is two columns already because it is an `open-form` HEADER ACTION, and CnActionButtons did forward both keys. Same app, same kind of record, two different forms, and no manifest key that explained the difference. nextcloud-vue 2.46.0 adds `formSize`/`formColumns` to CnIndexPage, CnDetailPage, CnObjectListWidget and CnObjectDataWidget, which is what these two keys reach.
config._includeFieldsNote: Twelve of the forty-one, and every one of them is also on CaseTypeDetail, so nothing here becomes unreachable by being left off the create form. The cut follows the detail page's own grouping: this is `case-type-core` (title, identifier, description, category, parentCaseType, purpose, trigger, handlingModel, confidentiality, isDraft) plus the two facts from `case-type-terms` that a type cannot sensibly start life without, its statutory `processingDeadline` and the `validFrom` it takes effect on. What is deliberately NOT here: the versioning trio (version, previousVersion, supersededBy) is written by the publish action, not typed; the relation lists (subCaseTypes, decisionTypes, relatedCaseTypes, startableFlows) are built up on the detail page once the thing they point at exists; the AVG block (case-type-privacy) is a data protection officer's pass over an existing type rather than an author's first screen; and the remaining specialist codings (layerIds, iv3TaskField, selectionListProcessType, referenceProcess, verwerkingsactiviteit) are lookups nobody has to hand while naming a new type. `initialStatus` is excluded for a HARDER reason, the same one the CaseTypes-adjacent `case` form records for `status`: it is a $ref to a statusType filtered by `caseType`, and at create time this case type has no id and therefore no statuses, so the picker would fetch unfiltered and offer every OTHER type's statuses. Half of those are called `Received` or `In progress`, which makes them both indistinguishable and wrong. A type's statuses are authored on its detail page, after it exists.
config._fieldOverridesNote: `order` is set here rather than on the register because fieldsFromSchema resolves an override's `order` AHEAD of the property's own, so one manifest map orders every schema-driven surface without a data-model change. It is not cosmetic: not one of caseType's 41 properties carries an `order`, so the sort falls through to alphabetical and a form that opens on `Category` puts `Title` TENTH. The three prose fields are declared `textarea` because caseType leaves them as plain strings with no maxLength, so resolveWidget renders a single-line input for what is a paragraph. That also decides the layout: CnFormDialog spans a textarea across BOTH columns (WIDE_WIDGETS), so the nine single-line fields pair up into rows first and the three prose fields follow full width, which is why the order puts them last. Interleaved, each one would leave the column beside it empty.
config._folderSidebarNote: `source: "field"` and not `source: "facet"`. CnIndexPage still resolves exactly four sources, register, field, custom and files, and CnFolderSidebar's own validator takes only custom, field and files, so a sidebar declared as a facet falls through to `custom`, finds the (absent) `folders` array and renders an empty pane. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS NOTE WAS TRUE UNTIL nextcloud-vue 2.42.0 AND IS NOT ANY MORE: `field` no longer derives the folders from the distinct `category` values of the loaded rows. Since #1036 it prefers the FACET for `field`, which is computed over the whole query with pagination stripped, and only groups the rows when no facet arrives. That is what makes a category reachable when every row carrying it sits on a later page, and it is why no manifest change is wanted here: `facetable: true` on the property plus `source: "field"` is the whole contract, and the object store adds `_facets=extend` on its own once the fetched schema has any facetable property. `x-openregister-facet` is still read by nothing. ⚠️ The facet ARRIVES an hour stale, because OpenRegister caches the response and no object write invalidates it, so a category added today gets no folder today: OpenRegister#3560, and the reason the folder e2e test is parked.
config._quickFiltersNote: The index used to list every version of every case type, so a catalogue of forty types read as a list of ninety rows carrying the same nine names three times over, and the row you wanted was whichever one had no successor. Current versions is the DEFAULT chip and carries `supersededBy: "IS NULL"`, the literal sentinel every OpenRegister condition builder matches by value, which the Queue page's `assignee: "IS NULL"` already relies on. It is a CHIP and not a base `filter` on the page, deliberately: a base filter cannot be cleared by the person reading the list, and the older versions are exactly what an auditor asking which rules governed a case last March came here for. All versions drops the condition and shows the whole chain. A draft has no successor either, so it sits under both chips, which is right: a draft is the version you are about to publish.

pages._note: A case type is the blueprint every case is governed by — lifecycle, deadlines, classification, the workflow that drives it — and `case.caseType` references it. It had no surface at all: the original `CaseTypesMenu` pointed at the in-app `/settings` page, which page-topology-cleanup B1 retired for mounting AdminRoot through the in-app router (ADR-004), and no replacement was ever built. The capability went with the page and only its stale `settingsSection` id was left behind. WorkflowDefinitionDetail's own note still says cases are 'reached through their caseType index', naming this page. Restored as an ordinary schema-driven index rather than by reviving the retired settings route.

pages.title: Attributes

config._showViewActionNote: There is no PropertyDefinitionDetail page and a view action with no route pushes vue-router at a name it cannot resolve, so the row opens the metadata sidebar instead. An attribute is eight fields; a page of its own would be the sidebar with a header.
config._folderSidebarNote: `source: "field"` and not `source: "facet"`: CnFolderSidebar's validator takes custom, field and files only, and a sidebar declared as a facet falls through to `custom`, finds no `folders` array and renders an empty pane. The shape is the one `#CaseTypes` carries. Since nextcloud-vue 2.42.0 the `field` source PREFERS the facet, which OpenRegister computes over the whole query with pagination stripped, so a category is reachable even when all of its attributes sit on a later page; `facetable: true` on `propertyDefinition.category` plus this block is the whole contract and the object store adds `_facets=extend` on its own. AN ATTRIBUTE WITH NO CATEGORY GETS ITS FOLDER FROM THE SCHEMA DEFAULT, not from this pane: `fieldTree()` skips a row whose grouping value is null, undefined or empty, so there is nowhere here to name an empty bucket, and `category` defaults to Uncategorised on the register instead. ⚠️ The facet arrives up to an hour stale, because OpenRegister caches the response and no object write invalidates it (OpenRegister#3560), so a category added today may get no folder today.

The filter is `identifier` and NOT a walk over `previousVersion`: two rows are versions of one zaaktype when they share ZGW's `identificatie`, and a walk answers a SHORTER list on a chain with a hole in it, where a version missing from the list reads as a version that does not exist. `@object.identifier` and not `@objectId`, because the filter compares the shared identifier rather than this row's own id. `rowRoute` points back at this same page, which is how you move between versions.

config._headerActionsNote: There is no `run-action` header-action type. The manifest schema enumerates handler, open-modal, open-page, navigate, object-op, export, open-form, refresh, api-call, agent and toggle, and CnActionButtons resolves exactly those; the design's `run-action` would have been refused by `npm run check:manifest` and, had it slipped through, rendered a button that dispatches nothing. Export is an `api-call` with `download: true`, which is the shape that asks for the response as a blob and hands it to the browser -- the endpoint already answers a DataDownloadResponse. The other three are dialogs, each for a reason a declarative action cannot meet: Import takes a FILE (a confirm gate has no fields and an api-call sends JSON), Publish must show the validation findings BEFORE asking for a change note, and Duplicate must land on the copy rather than refresh the page you are already on. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all. The three dialogs read the case type off the ROUTE and not off their props: `open-modal` forwards props verbatim, so a `@objectId` token would arrive as that literal string. case-type-version-chain adds two. NEW VERSION is a dialog and not the api-call its tasks named, for the reason Duplicate is one: an api-call refreshes the page you are already on, so the person who asked for a new version would be left on the old one with the draft nowhere in sight. It also says what a version IS before making one, because the gesture beside it is Duplicate: a duplicate is a second case type, a version is this one later on, same name, same identifier, and today's running cases stay where they are. DEPRECATE is an api-call to a dossiq endpoint and NOT the `object-op` the design named. An object-op merges its `values` into the row verbatim: `validUntil: "@today"` is not token-resolved for that action type, so the literal string `@today` would have been written into a date field and stored without complaint. The day comes from the server's clock instead, and the server also refuses to close a version nothing has replaced. Its `visibleWhen` is a SOURCE query rather than a local field test, because the local operator set is eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte with no is-set, and `supersededBy neq null` reads TRUE on an unset field, which is the opposite of what it means. Counting the published rows whose `previousVersion` is this one asks the same question and can answer it.

pages._note: ADR-080: the store plane. Discovery belongs to OpenRegister — this page reads /api/store/items, which is a thin action over AppHost's GenericStoreService, so the SSRF guard, the redirect refusal and the token live in the engine and dossiq builds no registry URL. The library store page (`type: "store"`, CnStorePage) and not type:index, because store items are REMOTE objects: the object-backed index renderer resolves a local register+schema and cannot address them. CnStorePage calls the same /apps/dossiq/api/store/items and /install, shows Install to administrators only, and the install action refuses anyone else on the server (AuthorizedAdminSetting). With no registry configured the engine answers not_configured WITHOUT a network call and the page renders dossiq's built-in templates, which is Decision 4 and the only reason this surface may carry the word Store at all. Install is dossiq's own and admin-guarded (Decision 3), and it writes case CONFIGURATION only — the record schemas are refused. PLACEMENT: footer, order 92, between Documentation (90) and Reports (95). openbuild, hermiq and integriq put Store in the main section instead; ADR-080 records no placement decision, so one of the two conventions is wrong and the ADR needs an amendment either way.

config._typeNote: The change's design (D2) asked for `type: "settings"`. The installed @conduction/nextcloud-vue dist cannot host this page there, and the reason is worth writing down rather than rediscovering. A `settings` section's `widgets[]` resolves ONLY against BUILTIN_SETTINGS_WIDGETS (`version-info`, `register-mapping`) and the `component` discriminator; `object-list` is a DASHBOARD widget (`registerDashboardWidget('object-list', …)`), so it would resolve to nothing, log one console warn and render an empty section. CnSettingsPage also takes no page-level `widgets[]` prop, so the uniform grid is not a way in either. Task 2.2 named this exact outcome and the interim it licenses: an `index` page over the config schema, never a `custom` page (the ADR-100 ratchet). The cost is REQ-ADMIN-021, the Required apps section, which needs `CnLeafDependencySettings` through a `type: "component"` widget, and that requirement stays red until a settings section can host a list. Nothing here needs to change when it can: the columns are the page, and the rows come from integriq's registry either way.
config._openSettingsNote: Open settings is a COLUMN with the built-in `link` widget, not a row action, because a row action cannot carry a per-row URL or a per-row visibility. `type: "navigate"` takes one literal `target` for the whole column and pushes it through vue-router, which cannot reach /settings/admin/dossiq at all; `handler` reaches the row but CnRowActions' `visible` predicate is a FUNCTION, which JSON cannot carry, and the action schema is additionalProperties:false so the key would be rejected anyway. The `link` widget substitutes `{settingsUrl}` from the row and, when that resolves to the empty string, `linkHref` is falsy and the cell falls through to plain text, which is exactly what REQ-ADMIN-019 asks for on the BRP, KvK, PDOK, Berichtenbox and Document templates rows: no Open settings offered. Integriq copies `settingsUrl` from lib/Settings/connections.json, where those five rows omit it.

observability._note: Declarative observability via OpenRegister's AppHost engine (ADR-040). Reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names (with the engine-added dossiq_ prefix), types, HELP texts and label keys (incl. the caseType JSON field surfacing as the case_type label) match the pre-adoption contract; the implicit dossiq_info / dossiq_up gauges are emitted by the engine. The APCu controller-local cache is replaced by the engine's per-metric cacheTtl via the distributed cache (same 30s/60s TTLs, shared across workers). 🔴 `dossiq_tasks_total` AND `dossiq_tasks_overdue_total` ARE GONE, and they are the one break in that parity. Both were `kind: objectCount` over `schema: caseTask`, and remove-casetask deleted the schema: a counter over a schema nothing declares reports 0 for ever, which on a task gauge reads as a quiet week rather than as a broken metric. Task counts belong to whoever owns the tasks, and that is now OpenRegister's task engine, which is exporting them itself in openregister#3597. An `objectCount` source cannot reach the engine's table, so there is nothing dossiq can declare here in the meantime.
